turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs Hale, if you just slip your arm out of that sleeve. Doctor's a few minutes behind, so I'll do the bits and bobs while we wait.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. Um, I only really came about my knee. Is the cuff necessary? I go a bit funny the second I sit in this room.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): It's the usual check, love, won't take a moment. There we are... one seventy-two over ninety-eight.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): One seventy-two? That's not my number. My heart's going, do I need an ambulance or something silly?
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Nobody's calling an ambulance off one reading. Sit back, feet flat, and I'll repeat it once you've had a breather. Have you ever been on a blood pressure tablet?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. I don't take anything. Well, actually, paracetamol now and then for the knee, that's all. Is one seventy-two a stroke reading?
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): I can't answer the stroke bit, the doctor will. Quiet for me... second one's one sixty-four over ninety-four. Still on the high side.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Still high. I knew it. It's white coat, it always is when I come here. My dad had a stroke, so the second anyone says blood pressure I just unravel.
[SEG0009] person_1 (NURSE): I'll pass both readings on. Any chest pain while you're sitting there?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. More a sort of tight thing when I'm wound up. I don't know. Sorry, that's not a proper answer, is it?
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Doctor Okonkwo. Sorry you've been waiting. Sounds like the knee got you through the door, and then the machine joined in.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Which of those numbers do you actually trust? And please don't say both, because that doesn't help my head.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): They were both taken properly, a few minutes apart, so I won't throw either away. Before we get stuck on them, tell me what the knee has been doing.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Right, um, it's the right knee. I was kneeling, weeding the front bed, and it started aching. That was maybe three weeks ago. Worse on the stairs.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it swell up, lock on you, or give way?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of that. It's stiff for a few minutes when I first get up, then it eases. I can still walk the dog, if that's useful.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Walking the dog counts. How bad is the ache, if ten is the worst pain you can imagine?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): A three. Maybe a four straight after gardening. Do I need a scan? And, sorry, the car park nearly sent me home, is three weeks too long to have waited?
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): The car park defeats everyone, and three weeks isn't late. I wouldn't scan this. Hop up and I'll have a look.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Please don't press too hard, I'm a bit of a wimp. Is it going to be arthritis? I'm fifty-four.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let's see before we name it. Right knee, no puffiness, it straightens and bends all the way, and it's a bit sore along the inner side. That the spot?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that's the spot. So is it arthritis? Fifty-four feels young for that.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): It feels more like wear and tear from the kneeling than anything I'd operate on. I'm not stamping a firm label on it this afternoon.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): So what do I actually do? I take two paracetamol when it's bad, not every day. Is that wrong? I'd rather not add more tablets.

[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Two when it aches is absolutely fine. I won't start a regular anti-inflammatory while the blood pressure's up in the air. Ice it after the garden, and don't kneel for long stretches.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): And you're really not starting a blood pressure tablet today, even with my dad? He was sixty-two when he had the stroke. I keep doing that sum in my head.

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): No tablet today. Your dad's stroke is worth knowing, but two readings in here, with a sore knee and you already rattled, is not me diagnosing high blood pressure. Pain, rushing in, the cuff itself, any of those can lift it, and I don't know which.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): So it might just be the white coat? Or the knee? Or me being anxious? I need it to be one thing.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): It might be any of those, or a mix, or a blood pressure problem we can't see properly in this room. I'm not picking one today. A week of your own readings will tell us more than another argument with the machine.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I haven't got a machine. Will you lend one, or is that the chemist? How many times, because I will get obsessed, I know I will.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll lend you one from the surgery. Morning and evening for seven days, sitting quietly, left arm each time. If a number looks daft, wait five minutes, repeat it, and write both down.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): What number means I ring you instead of waiting? And what if I do the cuff wrong and it's my fault?

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Over one-eighty, or a cracking headache with your vision changing, or chest pain that isn't just the worry, ring the surgery that day. If you feel properly unwell, it's nine nine nine. A slightly clumsy technique is still worth having.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Do I bring the sheet back to you, though? I don't want to explain my dad all over again to someone else.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back to me in one week with the diary and the monitor. We'll read them together. Nothing gets started unless the home numbers say we should.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): If they're all high, it will be tablets, won't it? I read they make you dizzy, and I drive over to my sister's on Tuesdays.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): If they're high, we talk about treatment then. I'm not choosing a medicine today, so I won't pretend to list side effects for one you may never take. Lots of people drive on blood pressure tablets.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, the ice, how long for? And can I still do Sunday? We've got open gardens, which is a silly thing to be fretting about, I know.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ten minutes, wrapped in a tea towel, not on bare skin. Sunday's fine if you use a kneeler or stand up often, and stop when it starts to complain.
[SEG0040] person_1 (NURSE): I'll fetch the monitor from the cupboard, it's an Omron, plus a sheet with morning and evening boxes. Bring both back next week, love.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I sit at the kitchen table or is the sofa alright? The sofa's the only place I actually unwind. Last question, I think.
[SEG0042] person_1 (NURSE): Table, not the sofa. Feet on the floor, back against the chair, and not straight after a brew or the dog walk.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's plenty for one visit. Knee as we said, no new tablets, and we'll make sense of the pressure from your own numbers. Try not to let every beep spook you.
